        How to read this
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR contour map is drawn at 894 ft. Contours are off by about (894 − pool). If pool is lower, real water is shallower than printed.
        • Temp is gauge water ~2 ft down (°F in the lead; °C here for reference). It isn’t air temp, and not every creek arm.
        • USGS values are provisional (params 62614 pool / 00010 temp) and can be revised. USGS-03228400.
        • Hoover is a drinking-water reservoir with a 10 hp / 10 mph limit and idle speed within 100 ft of shore. Keep wakes down and pack out trash.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 888 ft summer pool. Contours are off by about (888 − pool). If pool is lower, real water is shallower than printed.
        • No public water temp gauge on the lake, so the temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • Lake level comes from the US Army Corps of Engineers (Huntington District), posted every 15 minutes. It is provisional and can be revised. Corps Alum Creek page.
        • Alum Creek is a drinking-water reservoir. Unlimited horsepower on the south main lake, no wake on the north end; the Corps and ODNR mark the line at different roads, so follow the buoys.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s 2 ft contours are based on the 891.75 ft normal summer pool. Contours are off by about (891.75 − pool). Buckeye Lake is shallow, so a few inches matter.
        • The USGS gauge on Buckeye Lake measures level only. No public water temp gauge, so the temp slot says n/a.
        • USGS values are provisional (param 62614) and can be revised. USGS-395540082291600.
        • No wake within 300 ft of any land mass and in marked areas; unlimited horsepower elsewhere. Check Ohio’s BeachGuard for algae advisories before wading or swimming a dog.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • Full pool here is the City of Columbus dam crest, 848.5 ft. The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on 847.9 ft, so contours are off by about (847.9 − pool). If pool is lower, real water is shallower than printed.
        • No public water temp gauge: the USGS gauge at the dam reads level only, and the City says its reservoir temperatures are not monitored. The temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • USGS values are provisional (param 62614) and can be revised. USGS-03220500.
        • City of Columbus drinking-water reservoir: unlimited horsepower, 40 mph by day and 10 mph from sunset to sunrise, boats 22 ft or shorter, no personal watercraft, tubing or swimming, and idle speed within 100 ft of shore and bridges (City of Columbus).
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • Full pool here is the City of Columbus dam crest, 756.18 ft. The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on 757 ft, so contours are off by about (757 − pool). If pool is lower, real water is shallower than printed.
        • Temp is the USGS reservoir gauge (°F in the lead). It isn’t air temp, and not every cove.
        • USGS values are provisional (params 62614 pool / 00010 temp) and can be revised. USGS-03221500.

        • Temp is the USGS gauge at the lake (°F in the lead). It isn’t air temp, and not every channel.
        • USGS values are provisional (params 62614 pool / 00010 temp) and can be revised. USGS-03260500.
        • No horsepower limit; no wake within 300 ft of any shoreline, in channels and where marked (ODNR). Check Ohio’s BeachGuard for algae advisories before wading or swimming a dog.

        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 915 ft normal summer pool. Contours are off by about (915 − pool). ODNR lists a 5 ft winter drawdown to 910 ft for flood control, set by the Corps.
        • No public water temp gauge on the lake, so the temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • Lake level comes from the US Army Corps of Engineers (Huntington District), posted every 15 minutes. It is provisional and can be revised. Corps Delaware Lake page.
        • Unlimited horsepower (ODNR). Follow the posted no wake buoys, and check Ohio’s BeachGuard for advisories before swimming.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 810.5 ft summer pool. Contours are off by about (810.5 − pool). ODNR lists a 14 ft winter drawdown to 796 ft from Oct. 1 to Nov. 30 (refill Apr. 1 to May 15), set by the Corps, and says the level can change up to 20 ft.
        • No public water temp gauge on the lake (the Corps posts an outflow temp below the dam only), so the temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • Lake level comes from the US Army Corps of Engineers (Huntington District), posted every 15 minutes. It is provisional and can be revised. Corps Deer Creek Lake page.

        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 965 ft summer pool (2 ft contours, surveyed 2006). If the lake is down, real water is shallower than printed.
        • Electric motors only (ODNR). Check Ohio’s BeachGuard for advisories before swimming.
        • No public lake level or water temp gauge: no USGS or Corps gauge posts Knox Lake (the USGS Kokosing River gauge is on the river, not the lake), so the level and temp slots say not available. Nothing is estimated.

        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 1,202 ft summer pool (3 ft contours, surveyed 1999). ODNR lists a 24 ft maximum depth; the City of Mansfield says 40 ft depths are not uncommon. Use the map as a guide.
        • City of Mansfield water supply lake: idle speed, no wake on the whole lake (City code; ODNR’s page says 8 mph), no horsepower limit, no swimming.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation in feet as USGS posts it, not the depth of any hole or channel.

        • Lake level comes from USGS gauge 03141000 at Senecaville. It is provisional and can be revised. USGS-03141000.
        • 399 hp limit (MWCD). Idle or no wake inside the buoyed and shore zones. Check Ohio’s BeachGuard for advisories before swimming.
        • Pool is lake surface elevation in feet as the Corps posts it, not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 737 ft summer pool (3 ft contours, surveyed 1999). Contours are off by about (737 − pool).
        • No public water temp gauge on the lake, so the temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • Lake level comes from the US Army Corps of Engineers (Huntington District), posted every 15 minutes. It is provisional and can be revised. Corps Dillon Lake page.
        • Unlimited horsepower, with many coves no wake (ODNR). A Corps flood control lake: the Corps sets any winter drawdown. Check Ohio’s BeachGuard before swimming.
        • No public lake level or water temp gauge: no USGS or Corps gauge posts Lake Logan, so the level and temp slots say not available. Nothing is estimated.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 759 ft summer pool (3 ft contours, surveyed 2006). If the lake is down, real water is shallower than printed. ODNR lists an 18 ft maximum depth.

        • No public lake level or water temp gauge: no USGS or Corps gauge posts Salt Fork Lake, so the level and temp slots say not available. Nothing is estimated.

        • Pool is lake surface elevation in feet as the Corps posts it, not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 721 ft summer pool (5 ft contours, surveyed 1999). Contours are off by about (721 − pool).
        • No public water temp gauge on the lake, so the temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • Lake level comes from the US Army Corps of Engineers gauge at Tom Jenkins Dam, posted every 15 minutes. It is provisional and can be revised. Corps Tom Jenkins Dam page.
        • 10 hp limit; larger motors at idle or no wake speed only, and no jet drives (ODNR).
        • No public lake level or water temp gauge: no USGS or Corps gauge posts Dow Lake, so the level and temp slots say not available. Nothing is estimated.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 660 ft summer pool (3 ft contours, surveyed 2006). If the lake is down, real water is shallower than printed. ODNR lists a 33 ft maximum depth.

              What this site is

              • Unofficial Hoover-only fishing hub with night-dock atmosphere
              • Unofficial Ohio fishing hub with night-dock atmosphere: Hoover, Alum Creek, Buckeye Lake, O’Shaughnessy, Griggs, Indian Lake, Delaware Lake, Deer Creek Lake, Madison Lake, Knox Lake, Clear Fork Reservoir, Seneca Lake, Dillon Lake, Lake Logan, Salt Fork Lake, Burr Oak Lake and Dow Lake
              • Species pages with limit reminders from the ODNR 2026–27 rules
              • One example log entry, marked Example · not ODNR / City / USGS
              Night fishing can be dangerous in storms, heat, and low visibility. Wear a life jacket when it calls for it. 10 hp · drinking-water reservoir · license ages 16+.No wake on the north end · drinking-water reservoir · license ages 16+.No wake within 300 ft of shore · shallow lake, check algae advisories · license ages 16+.40 mph, 10 mph after sunset · idle within 100 ft of shore · drinking-water reservoir · license ages 16+.No wake within 300 ft of shore · shallow lake, check algae advisories · license ages 16+.Corps winter drawdown · check BeachGuard advisories · license ages 16+.Corps fall drawdown to winter pool · check BeachGuard advisories · license ages 16+.Electric motors only · check BeachGuard advisories · license ages 16+.10 hp limit · 18 in bass minimum · license ages 16+.Idle speed, no wake · water supply lake, no swimming · license ages 16+.399 hp limit · 15 in bass minimum · license ages 16+.Corps flood control lake · check BeachGuard advisories · license ages 16+.10 hp, 10 mph · check BeachGuard advisories · license ages 16+.Speed and ski zones · 4 bass a day, split by size · license ages 16+.10 hp limit · no bass 12 to 15 in · license ages 16+.10 hp limit · no bass 12 to 15 in · license ages 16+.               Park hours and notes

              City park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. (Columbus Rec and Parks); check posted signs before a night trip. Shoreline traced from a map, not for navigation.

              Alum Creek State Park and Corps of Engineers land: check posted hours and rules before a night trip. Unlimited horsepower on the south main lake, no wake on the north end. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              No wake within 300 ft of any land mass and in marked areas (ODNR fishing map). Check posted state park hours before a night trip. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              City park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. (Columbus Rec and Parks); check posted signs before a night trip. 40 mph by day, 10 mph from sunset to sunrise (City code), idle within 100 ft of shore and bridges. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Indian Lake State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. No horsepower limit, no wake within 300 ft of shore. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Delaware State Park hours are sunrise to sunset; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Unlimited horsepower. Corps of Engineers lake. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Deer Creek State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Unlimited horsepower. Corps of Engineers lake with a fall drawdown. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Madison Lake State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Electric motors only. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              ODNR Division of Wildlife fishing area: 10 hp limit, larger motors at no wake or idle only. Check posted signs before a night trip. The marina and carry-in pins are approximate, from the ODNR fishing map. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              City of Mansfield water supply lake: idle speed, no wake on the whole lake, shore fishing on the south and west shores only, no swimming. City code bars parking from dark to dawn outside designated camping areas, so check posted City signs before a night trip. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              MWCD lake: 399 hp limit, idle or no wake in buoyed and shore zones. MWCD areas close from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. except to people fishing, hunting or boating. MWCD lists five public launch ramps; the two pinned here have mapped coordinates. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Dillon State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Unlimited horsepower, many coves no wake, two ramps at the south end. Corps of Engineers lake. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Lake Logan State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. 10 hp limit, 10 mph speed limit, two ramps off Lake Logan Road. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Salt Fork State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Unlimited horsepower with speed and ski zones. ODNR lists eight ramps; the two pinned here have mapped coordinates. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Burr Oak State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. 10 hp limit, larger motors at idle only, no jet drives, four ramps. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.

              Strouds Run State Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. 10 hp limit, one ramp, shore fishing by the dam. Shoreline traced from OpenStreetMap, not for navigation.
